{{Top}}
{{Rhere|Revolution|the [[Revolution (vehicle)|Revolution]] [[wheel bike]] or the [[Wikipedia:Wii|Wii]] [[Star Wars video games|video game]] console, codenamed Revolution}}
[[File:MoonBlockade-TCG.png|thumb|right|300px|The Imperial fleet in orbit over a moon]]
{{Quote|We are approaching the planet Yavin. The Rebel base is on a moon on the far side. We are preparing to orbit the planet.|The [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station/Legends|Death Star]] intercom announcing the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]]|<ref name="Episode 4">{{Film|IV}}</ref>}}
An '''orbit''' was the state of an object moving around a celestial body. Around a [[Planet/Legends|planet]], a [[Starship/Legends|starship]] or [[Space station/Legends|space station]] in orbit held its position outside or just within the world's outer [[Atmosphere/Legends|atmosphere]]. The completion of one orbit was known as a '''revolution'''. The [[Infinite Empire/Legends|Infinite Empire's]] [[chronological circuitry]], which could be installed into [[Rakatan guardian droid]]s such as the [[Overseer (droid)|Overseer]] on [[Dantooine/Legends|Dantooine]], could detect how many revolutions have taken place and were used as a dating device. By the [[Time/Legends|time]] of the [[Jedi Civil War]], the Overseer had worked as a Rakatan guardian [[Droid/Legends|droid]] for ten revolutions, which [[Bastila Shan]] realized corresponded to 20,000 years.

Orbit was also the second phase in a [[Planetary assault tactics|planetary assault]] and covered the gaining control of the orbital space around the target planetary system and the strategic orbital placement of the units in the invasion fleet.

==Physics==
{{Quote|Actually, an orbit is a very delicate balance between a planet's gravity and a spacecraft's speed.|[[4B-X]]|<ref name="SWSA">''[[Star Wars Science Adventures: Emergency in Escape Pod Four]]''</ref>}}
Slipping into orbit required a delicate balance between the [[Starship/Legends|starship's]] straightforward movement and the [[Planet/Legends|planet's]] [[Gravity/Legends|gravity]]. While the [[Laws of Motion|First Law of Motion]] stated that a ship in motion should normally stay in the same motion, the planet's gravity would pull down on it. The perfect balance for orbiting was achieved when the pull was not strong enough to make the ship crash, and yet strong enough to keep it from flying away.<ref name="SWSA" />

==Two types of orbital assault==
According to military strategist [[Michael Unther]] of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], there were two main tactics within this phase: ''objective orbit'' and ''siege orbit''.

===Objective orbit===
[[File:PlanetaryBombardment-SWGTCG.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Imperial Star Destroyers and frigates bombard a planet from orbit]]
Objective orbit consisted in placing the entire invasion fleet in the space above one single objective like a [[Capital/Legends|capital]] or a [[Spaceport/Legends|starport]]. This would allow the invasion fleet to target key points while remaining safe from raids by small groups of defending ships, but also only allowed for the control of smaller areas. Moreover, this strategy did not allow the invasion fleet to control enemy supply lines. One strategy to reduce the number of objectives was simply to bombard cities and starports as well as industrial facilities.

===Siege orbit===
In a siege orbit, the units in the fleet are placed around the planet so as to prevent enemy ships from leaving and entering. Siege orbits thus reduced the number of logistic assets of the defenders and also allowed for the bombardment of enemy ground forces wherever they would concentrate.

Unther considered this a more risky alternative to the objective orbit, and argued that the orbital siege at the [[Battle of Hoth/Legends|Battle of Hoth]] was an example of the weaknesses of siege orbits as [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader's]] invasion force were somewhat handicapped due to [[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] [[Kendal Ozzel/Legends|Ozzel's]] mistake during the [[Planetary assault tactics|approach]] phase. Because the fleet came out of [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] too close to the [[Hoth/Legends|Hoth]] system, the fleet units had to rush to get to their assigned positions, giving them little time for deploying fighter escorts. Several [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel]] ships managed to escape the system before Imperial vessels had reached their planetary orbital positions.

===Defending forces===
An important aspect of this phase was, according to Unther, knowledge of the defending forces, as there were several different ways to defend a system from planetary assault. The unorthodox strategies of [[Carigan]] at the [[Battle of Bryx]] caused severe problems for the Imperial invasion fleet. The most common type of planetary defense, however, was the [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighter]]-based [[space-snipe]] strategy.
